segments.he: ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מַסְתִּיר פָּנִים מֵאִתָּנוּ כְּדֵי שֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר אֵלָיו
segments.en: All the above-mentioned evil factions [from the story of the Baal Tefilah — Master of Prayer] are the aspect of the fallen character traits — and they exist within every person and at all times, as is apparent to the senses from all the evil acts done under the sun on account of the flaws of the above evil traits. There are people who are excessively craving honor and run after honor enormously — and lose their eternal world and even this world for the sake of a little honor they wish to attain. This one wants to be honored through his wealth, to have a name and honor among princes and nobles. And this one wants to be honored and esteemed through his Torah and his service — and all his days schemes to be accepted as a rabbi and leader in a great city. And there are those in whom the trait of murder dominates greatly — such as actual murderers. Or those who are not actual murderers, but possess the aspect of murder — for they are disputatious and hateful and jealous, and pursue a person even unto his life. This too is an aspect of murder, and this form of murder is very prevalent in the world, G-d spare us. And so with the other factions, as is self-evident to the one who examines. And even within a single person there are aspects of all the above factions. For by nature a person possesses all the bad traits — jealousy, desire, honor, and other lusts and evil traits — that all derive from the above evil factions. Only that in this person one particular evil trait dominates more — and so he is named after that faction. And in another person a different evil trait dominates — so he is named after that other faction. And so for all. And whoever wishes not to deceive himself, and to think about the true eternal purpose — cannot merit this except when he merits to be from the holy faction of the holy Baal Tefilah. For only they chose the true and eternal purpose — which is prayer and songs and praises to G-d. And through prayer one merits to break all the bad character traits that exist in every person.

segments.he: ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּבְיָכוֹל מַסְתִּיר עַצְמוֹ מֵאִתָּנוּ כְּדֵי שֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר מֵעַצְמֵנוּ אֵלָיו כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא שֶׁעִקַּר הַבְּרִיאָה הָיְתָה רַק בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁלּא תּאכַל הַנְּשָׁמָה נַהֲמָא דְּכִסּוּפָא כַּיָּדוּעַ. אֲבָל מֵעצֶם גַּשְׁמִיּוּת הָעוֹלָם קָשֶׁה לָנוּ מְאד לְהִתְעוֹרֵר מֵעַצְמֵנוּ כָּרָאוּי. כִּי בְּכָל יוֹם יִצְרוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו וְכוּ' (קִדּוּשִׁין ל'): וּמֵחֲמַת זֶה הֲוָה מַה דַּהֲוָה שֶׁנִּתְרַחַקְנוּ בַּעֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְרַחַקְנוּ וְנֶחֱרַב בַּיִת רִאשׁוֹן וּבַיִת שֵׁנִי. וַעֲדַיִן מְרַקֵּד בֵּינָן וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְאָרֵךְ הַגָּלוּת בַּעֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ הָרַבִּים. וְעַל כֵּן עִקַּר הַתִּקּוּן עַל יְדֵי אֲמִירַת תְּהִלִּים בְּכַוָּנָה שֶׁכּוֹלֵל שְׁנֵי הַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת יַחַד וְכַנַּ"ל.
segments.en: And this is the essential blessing of Modim [the blessing of Thanksgiving in the Amidah]. And this is the aspect of the bowing in Modim. For the bowing and prostration with which one gives thanks to G-d when saved from the trouble of the soul — which is the essential trouble, Heaven forfend — is itself the aspect of the descent transformed into an ascent. For the descent is the aspect of falling — the aspect of "My feet had almost stumbled" [Tehillim 73:2] — and it is the aspect of "For our soul has bent down to the dust, our belly cleaves to the earth" [ibid. 44:26]. And then one must prostrate oneself before G-d in bowing and prostration, in supplication, prayer, and request — in the manner of "Let him put his mouth in the dust — perhaps there is hope" [Eichah 3:29]. And then when one is strong in this — as explained in our other discussions at length — one merits that the descent is transformed into a great ascent.

segments.he: שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה עִקַּר קַבָּלַת אֱמוּנַת הַיִּחוּד שֶׁאָנוּ מְקַבְּלִין עָלֵינוּ בְּכָל יוֹם שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִזְכֶּה לְהִתְקָרֵב אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ וּלְהִתְחַבֵּר וּלְהִכָּלֵל בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ תָּמִיד מִכָּל הַמְּקוֹמוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם עַד שֶׁנִּזְכֶּה לִגְאֻלָּה שְׁלֵמָה עַל יְדֵי מְשִׁיחַ צִדְקֵנוּ שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְהַשִּׂיג וּלְגַלּוֹת הַשַּׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַכּל יֵלְכוּ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה לַעֲסֹק בַּאֲמִירַת תְּהִלִּים וְהִתְבּוֹדְדוּת הַרְבֵּה הַרְבֵּה עַד שֶׁנִּזְכֶּה לְתַקֵּן הַכּל בְּחַסְדּוֹ הַגָּדוֹל יִתְבָּרַךְ: (שָׁם אוֹת יג):
segments.en: And this is the aspect of viduy [confession] — that one must mention the sins and transgressions explicitly with a full mouth, and mention in clear speech such shameful matters. But this itself is one's entire rectification. For since one confesses and says "I have sinned" — one thereby acknowledges that there is a Creator, One and eternal — blessed be He — and thereby one acknowledges the Torah of Moshe as true, that the One eternal Creator warned us through Moshe not to commit these sins, only that one's evil inclination overcame one — and one acknowledges that one sinned and erred in this. For certainly one had the strength to overcome it — yet even so, since one confesses the sins and seeks teshuvah and forgiveness, one is searching and seeking still: "Where is He?" — and through this is the essential elevation.
